changes_made.explanation: Normalized task name, removed duplicate BERT variants, removed incorrect outputs (paper focuses on assessment, not generation), added missing comparison models used in experiments.
Corrected answer from No to Yes since paper uses automatic metrics to evaluate CEFR level classification performance. Normalized metric names to standard capitalization.
No LLMs used as judges/evaluators in this paper - only used as base models for classification.
No human evaluation of generated outputs conducted in this paper - human annotation was only for corpus creation, not for model evaluation.

overall_notes: The paper focuses on sentence difficulty assessment (classification) rather than text generation, but qualifies as NLG evaluation research since it develops evaluation methods for text simplification quality. The main contribution is the CEFR-SP corpus and CEFR level classification model for assessing sentence difficulty in educational contexts.
